title: First power-on
summary: USB-C PD negotiated 9 V on the first try, but a MOSFET kept the board from fully powering on.
body:
Upon powering up the board for the first time, the USB-C PD controller got the 9 V I’d asked for instead of falling back to the default 5 V, which is great! Unfortunately, the display and all four charger LEDs were still dark.

Next, I tried powering the ESP32 directly. It shares a supply rail with the charging ICs, so that brought up the charger circuits too. Three LEDs lit up and one stayed dark. All four channels use the same circuit, and this was my first time soldering DFN ICs, so my guess is a bad solder joint on that IC.

I probed around the power path between the PD controller and the buck converter.

- I measured 9 V at the PD output and on the input side of the MOSFET.
- The 9 V stopped at the MOSFET. The buck converter had no input, so the 5 V rail stayed off.

I went back to the schematic to see how I was driving that gate. Turns out, I accidentally chose a P-channel MOSFET for a circuit that called for an N-channel part. I updated the schematic and found a drop-in N-channel replacement in the same SOIC-8 package.

I’m about to leave for my internship in Thailand, so the swap will have to wait until I get back to school. Once the new part is in, I’ll verify that USB-C power brings up the 5 V rail, and then test charging on all four channels.
